title: BPE vocab shard incompatibility - canary incident and rollback notes
content:
Summary:

During a staged canary rollout of model-rev 2024-11-18 (internal tag: rev-bpe-2.0) to 5% of inference traffic, we observed a spike in customer error rates and a subtle class of hallucination/regression for prompts containing rare unicode sequences. The canary was automatically rolled back after 27 minutes. This doc captures timelines, root cause analysis, mitigation steps, and required follow-ups.

Impact: 
- Affected traffic: ~5% (canary pool) for ~27 minutes.
- Symptoms: increased 5xxs and malformed token sequences in generated outputs for ~0.3% of canary requests.
- External customer impact: no major customer-reported incidents; a handful of internal integration tests flagged downstream parse failures.

Detection timeline (UTC):
- 2024-11-20 14:03: Canary rollout started (5% traffic) for rev-bpe-2.0.
- 2024-11-20 14:08: Alert: per-route error rate increase on route /v1/generate: baseline 0.2% -> 1.6%.
- 2024-11-20 14:10: SRE on-call paged; initial investigation launched.
- 2024-11-20 14:12: Observability: increased token mismatch logs in canary nodes (log marker: tokenizer:unknown-token-mapped).
- 2024-11-20 14:25: Quick triage: pattern indicates tokenizer produced different token ids for identical input compared to control (stable model).
- 2024-11-20 14:30: Automated rollback triggered by rollout policy (error rate >1% for 15m) — canary aborted.
- 2024-11-20 14:32: Canary pool drained; traffic routed back to stable variant.
- 2024-11-20 14:50: Post-rollback monitoring shows error rates returning to baseline.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Abort rollout and drain canary (automated).
- Disabled subsequent pipeline stages for rev-bpe-2.0 and placed tag on model registry entry to prevent accidental re-deploy.
- Flushed tokenizer cache on canary hosts and invalidated KV prefixes to remove stale encodings.
- Added emergency blocking spectest in CI to reject any model that changes tokenization mapping for a canonical set of unicode test vectors.

Investigation & Root cause (summary):
- Root cause: a packaging change introduced in the tokenizer build step changed the shard boundary serialization for the BPE vocab (endianness + header bytes). Some canary workers loaded the new shard files while others fell back to an older cached artifact due to a parallel rollout of tokenizer assets. The mismatch caused identical inputs to be tokenized into different token id sequences depending on which host served the request. That leads to misaligned KV cache hits, incorrect past-key-values, and eventually malformed decoding for affected requests.
- Contributing factors:
  - Tokenizer assets are deployed asynchronously and not strictly version-pinned to the model artifact in the canary flow.
  - No deterministic tokenization regression test in the pre-rollout CI for multi-host consistency across binary shard formats.
  - Cache layering in the serving runtime assumes tokenizer determinism and did not detect cross-host token id drift.

Evidence collected:
- Comparison of token id sequences for input sample "​var-Ω-ç-微" on stable vs canary nodes:
  - stable token ids: [1043, 8251, 12, 99103]
  - canary token ids: [1043, 8249, 12, 99103]
  - Diff: single id divergence at index 1 for specific byte boundary.
- Binary header analysis of tokenizer shard files shows differing magic bytes and a swapped endianness flag between artifact v1 and v2.
- Host-level logs show a race where worker A fetched shard v2 from CDN while worker B used local cached v1 leading to mixed shards in the pool.

Why this caused errors (technical):
- Token id mismatch produced inconsistent KV cache keys; autoregressive decoding expects consistent past-key-values keyed by token id. Mismatched ids produce stale or wrong cache entries which can cause attention misalignment and occasional model perplexities and malformed token outputs, surface as increased 5xxs when downstream parsing fails.

Short-term remediation checklist (done):
- Rollback model rollout (done).
- Block redeploy of tokenizer artifact v2 until analysis complete (done).
- Invalidate CDN and local caches for tokenizer artifacts to enforce consistent repull (done).
- Add canary-level defensive check: compare token id sequences against control on a small sample of canonical inputs before opening traffic to >1% (implemented).

Longer-term corrective actions (action items):
- Add artifact pinning: require tokenizer artifact hash to be recorded and enforced in model registry entries (owner: Ravi Singh, due: 2024-12-05).
- CI smoke test: deterministic tokenization matrix across multiple host OS/endianness/worker configs (owner: Mariana Lopes, due: 2024-12-01).
- Serving runtime: detect and reject mixed-tokenizer-id traffic by adding a token-id-signature check at request ingress and log mismatches with higher fidelity (owner: Noah Kim, due: 2025-01-10).
- Runbook update: expand model rollout checklist to include tokenizer artifact checksum verification and CDN cache invalidation steps (owner: Evelyn Chen, due: 2024-12-01).
- Add telemetry metric: token-id-drift-rate per host to surface early divergence (owner: Ibrahim Al-Masri, due: 2024-12-12).

Runbook draft edits (snippet):
- "Pre-rollout checklist: confirm tokenizer artifact hash matches model registry entry; purge CDN and force-consistent pull across canary hosts; run tokenization-consistency test across 10+ sample inputs; ensure cache warmup and deterministic signature is present before opening >1% traffic."

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Why did CDN return mixed versions during the canary window? Was there a cache TTL misconfiguration or an atomic publish failure? (investigation: infra/cdn team).
- Should we always bundle tokenizer artifacts inside the model package (single deployable)? Pros/cons and storage/latency tradeoffs.
- Evaluate whether existing KV cache keying should include an explicit tokenizer artifact id to prevent silent cross-host contamination.

Appendix: Useful commands and logs
- Command to checksum tokenizer artifact currently in registry: shasum -a 256 /artifacts/tokenizer-v2.tar.gz
- Example diff command used in triage: python tools/token-diff.py --input test_vectors/core_unicode.txt --host-a canary-host-12 --host-b stable-host-04 > /tmp/token-diff.out
- Representative log lines:
  - 2024-11-20T14:11:23Z [tokenizer] host=canary-12 token_map_mismatch input_hash=0x9f3a msg="token id 8249 != 8251"
  - 2024-11-20T14:13:01Z [serving] host=canary-07 cache_miss=KV:0x3b4e reason="token-id-key-mismatch"

Notes for postmortem:
- Severity classification: P2 (partial regression confined to canary, automated rollback, no wide customer impact).
- We should schedule a cross-team postmortem review with packaging, infra/CDN, serving-runtime, and SRE to nail down the publish/atomicity failure mode.

Draft timeline for postmortem meeting:
- 2024-11-27 15:00 UTC: initial incident review (30 mins)
- 2024-12-04 16:00 UTC: technical deep-dive w/ infra and packaging (60 mins)

Last notes:
- This incident highlights an operational assumption violation: tokenizer format is a "hidden" dependency of the serving runtime and model behavior. We should treat tokenizer artifacts as first-class deployables and ensure deterministic behavior across hosts before any model rollout.

Document owner: Evelyn Chen
Reviewed by: Ravi Singh, Mariana Lopes
